_metadata.description: Own kernel session lifecycle: creation, grants, kernel state persistence across submissions, ceilings, reclamation, and optional sandbox binding.

requirements.title: Session-persistent kernel state
requirements.description: While a session is live, the Program Runtime MUST preserve kernel variable state across separate program submissions so a later program can reference an earlier program's handles.

validation.notes: Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestVariablesSurviveSubmissionBoundary` (tag the test [REQ:PRT-P0-004]). A handle bound in one submission is referenceable by name in a later submission on the same session.

Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestSessionsAreIsolatedFromEachOther` (tag the test [REQ:PRT-P0-004]). State bound in one session is not reachable from another, so concurrent agents cannot observe each other.

requirements.title: Sandbox composition
requirements.description: The Program Runtime SHOULD bind a session to a workspace-sandbox workspace so filesystem effects are isolated and reviewable.

validation.notes: Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestSessionBindsToSandboxWorkspace` and `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestSessionRejectsUnknownSandboxWorkspace` (tagged [REQ:PRT-P1-004]). A declared workspace is resolved before persistence and an unknown workspace is rejected with ErrInvalidWorkspace.

Target `api/internal/programs/runner_test.go::TestSubprocessRunnerUsesResolvedWorkspaceRoot` (tag the test [REQ:PRT-P1-004]). A session kernel's cwd is the resolved workspace root and the external workspace is not removed during runner cleanup.

requirements.title: Bounded session lifecycle
requirements.description: The Program Runtime SHOULD enforce idle reclamation and wall-clock and memory ceilings per session, and SHOULD report the reason when it reclaims a session.

validation.notes: Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestReclaimsIdleSessionWithStatedReason` (tag the test [REQ:PRT-P1-005]). An idle session past its ceiling is reclaimed and the reclamation reason is readable afterward.

Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestEnforcesWallClockAndMemoryCeilings` (tag the test [REQ:PRT-P1-005]). Wall-clock and memory ceilings terminate a session deterministically rather than degrading the host.

requirements.title: Per-session inference spend ceiling
requirements.description: The Program Runtime SHOULD enforce a configurable per-session ceiling over ai-gateway Usage.cost_micros, input tokens, and output tokens, and SHOULD report inference_spend_exceeded when the ceiling reclaims or refuses work.

validation.notes: Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestInferenceUsageAccumulatesAndCeilingRejects` (tagged [REQ:PRT-P1-010]) and `TestSessionWithoutInferenceCeilingRemainsUnlimited`. Session usage and ceilings are persisted and the bridge rejects further inference at the named ceiling.

requirements.title: Per-session delegated-run spend ceiling
requirements.description: The Program Runtime SHOULD enforce a separate configurable per-session ceiling over agent-manager delegated-run spend, and SHOULD report delegated_run_spend_exceeded when that ceiling reclaims or refuses work.

validation.notes: Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestDelegationSpendReceiptAccumulatesAndCeilingRejects` (tagged [REQ:PRT-P1-011]). Agent Manager publishes a terminal per-execution ChargeReceipt with currency, metering basis, and measured/unmeasured semantics; Program Runtime records measured receipts and atomically refuses a charge that would cross the delegated-run ceiling with delegated_run_spend_exceeded.

requirements.title: Named durable workspaces
requirements.description: The Program Runtime MAY support named sessions that survive across agent runs so a long investigation reuses accumulated state.

validation.notes: Target `api/internal/sessions/manager_test.go::TestNamedSessionSurvivesAcrossAgentRuns` (tag the test [REQ:PRT-P2-003]). A named session is resumable by a later agent run with its accumulated state intact.
